improvements.root_cause_title: Aggregate accumulation performs a fully generalized per-row NUMERIC add/mul (buffer zeroing, byte<->word conversion, precision recomputation, overflow check, round-and-pack, DB_VALUE construction) instead of a deferred-carry fast sum accumulator
improvements.evidence_event: heap rows scanned = 59,986,052 (identical both engines); denominator = total_query_cpu core-seconds per row, and retired instructions per row
improvements.explanation: PostgreSQL accumulates SUM/AVG into a 32-bit digit array with separate positive/negative buffers and propagates carry only once every NBASE-1 values, so the per-row cost is an int32 add per digit with no allocation, no precision recomputation and no rounding; CUBRID calls the general NUMERIC operator per row per aggregate, which memsets three VLA word buffers, converts both operands byte<->word, recomputes decimal precision, checks overflow, rounds/packs and builds a DB_VALUE.
improvements.effect_range: Bounded by the expression/NUMERIC/DB_VALUE band that dominates both profiles. CUBRID spends 62.35% of profiled self cost there while retiring 2.949x the instructions per row at 1.073x better IPC, so this band carries the majority of the 2.74x total-query-CPU gap. A deferred-carry accumulator cannot remove the scan/deform cost, so the realistic ceiling is a large fraction of the aggregate band, not of the whole query.
improvements.implementation_direction: Introduce an aggregate-local fixed-point sum accumulator for NUMERIC SUM/AVG that defers carry propagation and precision/overflow normalization to finalization, keeping the general operator only for the final materialization; avoid per-row DB_VALUE construction inside qdata_evaluate_aggregate_list.
improvements.correctness_risk: Must preserve CUBRID NUMERIC precision/scale and overflow semantics exactly, including the DB_MAX_NUMERIC_PRECISION rounding rule and the -0 normalization; deferred carry changes intermediate representation only, not the final rounded result.
improvements.validation_criteria: Q01 result must remain byte-identical for sum_qty/sum_base_price/sum_disc_price/sum_charge and within the SSOT 1e-12 relative rule for avg_*; re-run the section 11 gate plus a NUMERIC overflow/precision regression set; F_cpu must drop with F_work held at 1.0000.
improvements.priority_justification: Carries the majority of the measured F_cpu 2.7407x gap (186.67 vs 68.11 core-s), bounded by the 62.35% expression/NUMERIC/DB_VALUE profile band; largest single measured effect candidate for Q01.
improvements.difficulty_reason: Not a localized early-return: requires a new aggregate-local deferred-carry accumulator state, dispatch changes in the qdata_evaluate_aggregate_list path to bypass the generic qdata_add_dbval operator, and consistency with the parallel partial-aggregate merge path.
improvements.upstream_precedent: None identified in this investigation; report.md cites no prior CBRD issue/PR of the same kind. Code/issue-history survey needed.
improvements.ranking_rationale: Ranked above IMP-002: evidence band is 62.35% of CUBRID profiled self cost and directly explains most of F_cpu 2.7407x, versus IMP-002's <1%-of-query-CPU upper bound in this WARM regime (device read_bytes=0). Rejected sibling explanations and their rejecting numbers: plan shape (F_plan 1.0000 structural equality), parallelism (F_units 1.0197), work volume (F_work 1.0000 exact), memory stalls (CUBRID IPC 2.527 vs PG 2.354, i.e. 1.073x better while retiring 2.949x instructions per row).

improvements.root_cause_title: Data buffer replacement gives ~0% reuse for a repeated sequential scan whose working set slightly exceeds the buffer pool, where PostgreSQL retains a protected resident fraction
cubrid_source: src/storage/page_buffer.c (pgbuf victim selection / LRU zones; pgbuf_get_victim, pgbuf_unlatch_void_zone_bcb observed in profile)
postgresql_source: src/backend/storage/buffer/freelist.c (BufferAccessStrategy BAS_BULKREAD ring for large sequential scans)
improvements.evidence_event: data pages fetched per run vs pages read from outside the buffer pool
improvements.explanation: CUBRID trace reports fetch=682,982 and ioread=682,950 for the lineitem scan, i.e. essentially every page fetch missed the 8192MB buffer, because the 682,937-page (10.42 GiB) heap exceeds the 524,288-page pool and plain LRU evicts pages before reuse; PostgreSQL under the same equal 8192MB budget kept 694,494 of 1,125,128 blocks resident (61.7% hit) because the bulk-read ring protects the resident set from scan-driven eviction.
improvements.effect_range: UPPER BOUND < 1% of CUBRID query CPU under the current WARM regime. Because device read_bytes is 0 on both engines, every miss is served from the OS page cache, and the measured page-fetch path is small: pgbuf_get_vpid_ptr 0.19%, pgbuf_unlatch_void_zone_bcb 0.06%, pgbuf_get_victim 0.06%, kernel filemap_get_read_batch 0.13% + filemap_read 0.07%. The 6.06% heap_attrinfo_read_dbvalues is tuple deform, not page fetch, and is NOT attributed here. This candidate would only become material with a cold OS page cache, which is outside the section 12 WARM regime.
improvements.implementation_direction: Consider a scan-resistant replacement policy or bulk-read ring for large sequential scans so a repeated scan retains a resident fraction instead of self-evicting; do not pursue on Q01 CPU grounds alone.
improvements.correctness_risk: None expected; replacement policy does not affect results. Risk is regression for workloads that rely on current LRU promotion.
improvements.validation_criteria: Buffer hit ratio > 0 on a repeated scan of a table 1.0-1.5x the pool size, with no regression in the section 11 correctness gate and no increase in Q01 median wall.
improvements.priority_justification: Upper bound < 1% of CUBRID query CPU in the mandated WARM regime: device read_bytes=0 on both engines and the measured page-fetch path totals under 1% (pgbuf_get_vpid_ptr 0.19%, pgbuf_unlatch_void_zone_bcb 0.06%, pgbuf_get_victim 0.06%, kernel filemap 0.20%).
improvements.difficulty_reason: A scan-resistant replacement policy is a structural change: victim-selection/zone-promotion logic in page_buffer.c plus plumbing scan-context awareness from the executor down to the buffer manager, not a localized fix.
improvements.upstream_precedent: No precedent identified in this investigation; report.md cites no prior CBRD issue/PR of the same kind.
improvements.ranking_rationale: Ranked below IMP-001: despite the dramatic 0.005% buffer hit ratio (ioread 682,950 / fetch 682,982), device read_bytes=0 rejects any material CPU contribution in this WARM regime, which is why this is filed as a separate upper-bound item and not folded into the F_cost decomposition; IMP-001's 62.35% band dominates. Effects are disjoint (page replacement vs aggregate accumulation) and are not summed.
